citation.authors: Cheong JM, A Halim NA, Mohammad N, Sivagnanam M, Mohd Ibrahim MS
citation.title: Establishing H Angle Hard Tissue and H Angle Soft Tissue Norms in Skeletal Class I Malay Adult Females and the Correlation between the H Angles and Visual Perception of Laypersons

curation.notes: Compared 2026-10-08 (norms:compare a vs b exit 1, 2 differences, source wording; logs/task9b2-compare-cheong2024.log). H-angle 15.75 ± 4.16 and ANB 3.15 ± 0.77 agree and were re-read from Table 1 with the PubMed full-text tool (PMC11750322, DOI 10.1055/s-0044-1787005; rule P44, text not saved). Decisions: ANB not entered although both extracted it (P45: ANB 1-5° was an inclusion criterion, so its spread is cut by the selection) -> caveat with its value (merge notes). H angle hard tissue (NB to H-line) is not catalogue #80 -> caveat. Source 'Table 1, PMC11750322' (the PMC text has no page numbers). Selection class-I (ANB 1-5°; no profile or occlusion criterion). Scale not-stated (angles only).

caveats: Women only (n 85, Malaysian Malay, 20-40 y, mean 28.6 ± 5.86); no values for men.
Not entered: ANB 3.15 ± 0.77° (Table 1). ANB 1-5° was an inclusion criterion, so its spread is cut by the selection and it would make normal patients look abnormal (P45).
Not in the catalogue: H angle hard tissue (NB line to H line), Table 1: 11.64 ± 4.71°.

Pretreatment films of patients who sought orthodontic treatment, mainly for facial appearance and smile, from two private clinics (convenience sample, October 2017-December 2021); selected for a Class I skeletal pattern (ANB 1-5°) only, not for normal occlusion or a balanced profile.
Hand traced on acetate by one examiner; natural head posture with FH parallel to the floor; no magnification statement (only an angle is entered).

entries.note: The paper's 'H angle soft tissue': the soft-tissue facial line (N′–Pg′) to the H line (tangent to the upper lip and soft-tissue pogonion), Holdaway 1983. Printed unsigned; a positive angle of this size is the upper lip ahead of the soft-tissue facial line, the catalogue's positive direction.
